data.name: Balaansh
data.gender_notes: Balaansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Balaansh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'Bala' meaning strength and 'Ansh' meaning form or symbol. This name is given to a child who is believed to embody the qualities of a brave hero. In Hindu mythology, Balaansh is the name of Lord Shiva's son, who is a symbol of power and courage. The name Balaansh carries the meaning “Strong, Brave, Hero” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Balaansh usually hope their child will grow to embody strong, brave, hero and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the inner strength and courage of an individual.
data.etymology: Balaansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Strong, Brave, Hero.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Balaansh total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Balaansh was the name of a Jain Tirthankara who lived around 1st century BCE in the southwestern Indian state of Karnataka. He is considered a great conqueror of desires, as indicated by his name which means 'one who subdues or conquers the senses'. His teachings emphasized simplicity, non-violence, and detachment.

Balaansh is also the name of a Hindu deity, specifically a form of Lord Subrahmanyan or Murugan. In Hindu mythology, Balaansh is depicted as a child riding on a peacock and carrying a mace and a bow. He is worshipped for protection from diseases and for success in undertakings.
